newsitem.title: UK: Direct Line full year pre-tax profits sink.
newsitem.headline: Direct Line full year pre-tax profits sink.

text.p: Royal Bank of Scotland Plc said on Thursday that full year pre-tax profits at its Direct Line Insurance subsidiary fell 86 million pounds ($144.4 million) to 26 million due to difficult trading conditions.
"General insurance premium income at Direct Line showed little growth, reflecting the lower motor premium rates in the industry," Royal Bank of Scotland said in a results statement.

Motor insurance premiums were five percent lower than in the previous year and the total number of policies remained at the 1995 level of 2.2 million. Household insurance policies increased to 0.8 million from 0.7 million.

Royal Bank of Scotland said general insurance claims at Direct Line increased by 114 million pounds to 562 million because of volume growth, the effects of severe winter weather and a rise in the average cost of personal injury claims.

"Nevertheless, during a period of exceptional competition in UK motor insurance, Direct Line sustained its leading position," said Royal Bank of Scotland chairman Lord Younger. "Direct Line will benefit once premium rates recover."
Operating cost per policy fell from 48 pounds to 45 in the year to end September. Staff numbers at Direct Line Insurance were cut from 2,850 to 2,690 over the year. ($1=.5956 pound)
